source_refs.note: Vector or Cross Product: a main subheading of 2.3 Product of two vectors, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 25-25.

blocks.text: The vector product of two vectors A⃗ and B⃗, is a vector which is defined as

blocks.text_alt: A⃗ × B⃗ = AB sin θ n̂   (2.9)

blocks.text: where n̂ is a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing A⃗ and B⃗ as shown in Fig. 2.4 (a). Its direction can be determined by right hand rule. For that purpose, place together the tail of vectors A⃗ and B⃗ to define the plane of vectors A⃗ and B⃗. The direction of the product vector is perpendicular to this plane. Rotate the First vector A⃗ into B⃗ through the smaller of the two possible angles and curl the fingers of the right hand in the direction of rotation, keeping the thumb erect. The direction of the product vector will be along the erect thumb, as shown in the Fig 2.4 (b). Because of this direction rule, B⃗ x A⃗ is a vector opposite in sign to A⃗ x B⃗ (Fig. 2.4-c). Hence,

blocks.alt: Vectors A and B lie in a shaded plane with angle theta between them. A x B points straight up from their common tail, perpendicular to the plane; a small arrow beside it marks the unit vector n-hat, and a curled arrow round A x B shows the sense of rotation from A to B.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(a): The vector product A × B, along n̂ perpendicular to the plane of A and B (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.4(a)).

blocks.alt: The same plane with A, B and theta. Above it a right hand with the fingers curled from A towards B and the thumb erect; the thumb points along n-hat, the same way as A x B.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(b): Right-hand rule for the direction of A × B (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.4(b)).

blocks.alt: The plane with A, B and theta, the rotation now from B into A. B x A points straight down from the common tail, opposite to A x B, with a curled arrow round it.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(c): B × A is opposite to A × B (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.4(c)).

blocks.alt: Vectors A and B drawn from one point at angle theta form two sides of a shaded parallelogram; the other two sides are dashed.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(d): The parallelogram formed with A and B as adjacent sides (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.4(d)).
